How FALAJ turns Abu Dhabi flight data into hotel-demand forecasts
DATA  →  MODEL  →  VALIDATION  →  BACKEND  →  FRONTEND
The question
When flights change, what happens to hotel demand?
FALAJ links airport arrivals to hotel guest nights, before the change lands.

Flights describe the supply of seats. Hotel files describe the demand. FALAJ joins them by market.
2 · Clean and join
Check the data, then build one panel
✕ 19 rows removed: load factor above 120%, private, cargo and unknown operators
✓ passengers = P2P + transfer + transit: 0 errors
✓ no duplicates · no arrivals above guests
Market × month panel
Every market-month is compared with the same month one year earlier, so seasonality is built in.
3 · The forecasting model (L2)
Predict the change from last year
ln(GNthis yr / GNlast yr) = α + β·Δln Seats + γ·ΔRamadan + δ·ΔEid
α · TREND
0.106
≈ +11% a year before any change
β · SEATS
0.52
10% more seats → ~5% more nights
γ · RAMADAN
−0.28
full Ramadan month → ~25% fewer
δ · EID
−0.03
small · not significant

Train on the past → forecast the next month → compare with reality · origin 1 of 19
Error on the Abu Dhabi monthly total · lower is better

80% ranges held 80% of real outcomes

19 rolling forecasts, Jan 2024 – Jul 2025, using each month's known seat schedule.
5 · Second engine: daily nowcast
Guests today = people who arrived and haven't left
International daily error 12.7% vs 29.8% same weekday last year
Domestic daily error 8.4% vs 19.9% same weekday last year
Used only when arrivals are already known · it fills the Aug 2025 – Feb 2026 test period.

8 · Honest by design
What the numbers mean, and what they don't
Association, not cause
Airlines add seats where demand is already growing. We show the link and its range, not a guarantee.
Known seats in testing
The back-test uses each month's real schedule. In planning, the seat plan is the planner's input.
Trust the total most
About 6% error on the Abu Dhabi total, about 18% for a single market. Grades A/B/C say which to trust.
Shocks need a planner
Events like the 2026 disruption aren't in the data. Planners enter the seats they expect.
